allow.why: the loop over standard input of the compiled model harness/v2/lean_differential.py runs; no theorem is about it

theorems.name: BlazeGraph.Ledger.fnv1a_from_returns
theorems.says: With more fuel than bytes, the functional model of blaze_graph::ledger::fnv1a_from returns FNV-1a's fold of the seed over the bytes.

theorems.name: blaze_graph.ledger.fnv1a_from.spec.proof
theorems.says: The statement blaze generates from fnv1a_from's ensures holds of its model: it does not panic, and of no bytes it returns its seed.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.step_deterministic
theorems.says: A state has one next outcome: the semantics of MIR is deterministic.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.run_mono
theorems.says: A run that ends (a value, a panic or undefined behaviour) ends the same with any more fuel.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.run_agree
theorems.says: Two runs of one state that both end give the same outcome, whatever their fuel.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.State.read_write_other
theorems.says: The frame lemma: a write at a place leaves the read of every place in another slot as it was.

theorems.name: BlazeGraph.LedgerMir.fnv1a_from_model_agrees
theorems.says: The functional model of fnv1a_from and the semantics of its MIR body give the same outcome, for every seed and slice, with 4 * len + 5 steps or more.

theorems.name: BlazeGraph.LedgerMir.fnv1a_from_any_fuel
theorems.says: With any fuel, the MIR of fnv1a_from is out of fuel or returns the fold: it never panics and has no undefined behaviour.

theorems.name: BlazeAgrees.arith.add_one.agrees
theorems.says: The model of arith::add_one and the semantics of its MIR give the same outcome, the value or the overflow panic, for every argument.

theorems.name: BlazeAgrees.early.clamp.agrees
theorems.says: The model of early::clamp and the semantics of its MIR give the same value on both branches, for every argument.

theorems.name: BlazeAgrees.loops.count.agrees
theorems.says: The model of loops::count and the semantics of its MIR give the same value, for every argument, by the loop lemma run_loop.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.run_mapBlocks
theorems.says: A rewrite that leaves each block's meaning as it was from every state preserves every run, with the same fuel.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Sim.run
theorems.says: A lockstep simulation through a map on states, under an invariant it keeps, gives equal runs for every fuel.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.removeStorageMarkers_correct
theorems.says: The program without storage markers runs as the program does, for every fuel and state.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.simplifyConstCondition_correct
theorems.says: A switchInt or an assert on a constant made a goto runs as before, for every fuel and state.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.removeNops_correct
theorems.says: The program without nops runs as the program does, for every fuel and state.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.constFold_correct
theorems.says: A binary, checked or unary operation or a cast on constants replaced by its value runs as before; one that panics is left.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.validate_sound
theorems.says: The normal-form validator is sound: a pair of programs it accepts runs alike for every fuel and state.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.execStmt_ctl
theorems.says: A statement leaves control as it was: which function each frame runs, the block it is at, and the block its caller goes on at.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.execStmt_rename
theorems.says: A statement commutes with a renumbering of blocks: from the renamed state it gives the renamed state.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.step_rename
theorems.says: One step of a renumbered program from the renamed state is the renamed step of the program, at every block the renumbering keeps.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Renumbers.sim_total
theorems.says: A renumbering that keeps every block is a lockstep simulation, with no invariant.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.step_reaches
theorems.says: The reachability invariant (control is at a live block and returns to live blocks) is kept by every step, when the live blocks are closed under jumps.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Renumbers.sim_live
theorems.says: A renumbering that keeps only a closed set of live blocks is a lockstep simulation on the states the reachability invariant holds of.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.permuteBlocks_correct
theorems.says: A checked permutation of each function's blocks runs as the program does, for every fuel and every state.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.permuteBlocks_call
theorems.says: A checked permutation of blocks gives every call the same outcome.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.removeDeadBlocks_correct
theorems.says: Dead-block removal, when its check passes, runs as the program does from every state the reachability invariant holds of.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.removeDeadBlocks_call
theorems.says: Dead-block removal, when its check passes, gives every call the same outcome.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Stutter.run_target
theorems.says: Under a stuttering simulation with bound K, a target run of n steps that ends is the source's run of K * n steps.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Stutter.run_source
theorems.says: Under a stuttering simulation, a source run of n steps that ends is the target's run of n steps.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.threadGotos_target
theorems.says: A run of the goto-threaded program that ends in n steps is the program's run of 2 * n steps.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.threadGotos_source
theorems.says: A run of the program that ends in n steps is the goto-threaded program's run of n steps.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.threadGotos_call_source
theorems.says: A call that ends in n steps gives the same outcome in the goto-threaded program.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.threadGotos_call_target
theorems.says: A call of the goto-threaded program that ends in n steps gives the same outcome in the program with 2 * n steps.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.threadGotosN_target
theorems.says: After k rounds of goto threading, a run that ends in n steps is the program's run of 2 ^ k * n steps.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.threadGotosN_source
theorems.says: A run of the program that ends in n steps is the run of n steps after any number of rounds of goto threading.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.run_refines
theorems.says: When every step of the target refines the step of the source, every run of the target refines the run of the source, with the same fuel.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.switchToGoto_refines
theorems.says: A switchInt whose arms all go to one block made a goto refines the program: the same run, unless the program's is undefined.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.execStmt_mapStack
theorems.says: A statement commutes with any map on the stack that leaves memory alone.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.execBlockFrom_top
theorems.says: A block that does not end in a call does the same whatever block the running frame is at.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.mergeGotos_target
theorems.says: A run of the block-merged program that ends in n steps is the program's run of 2 * n steps, for every choice of targets merged.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.mergeGotos_source
theorems.says: A run of the program that ends in n steps is the block-merged program's run of n steps.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.mergeGotos_call_source
theorems.says: A call that ends in n steps gives the same outcome in the block-merged program.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.threadAll_target
theorems.says: With every target threaded, a call's return target too, a run that ends in n steps from the mapped state is the program's run of 2 * n steps.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.threadAll_source
theorems.says: A run of the program that ends in n steps is the run of n steps of the program with every target threaded, from the mapped state.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.threadAll_call_source
theorems.says: A call that ends in n steps gives the same outcome with every target threaded.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.State.read_ok
theorems.says: When every pointer in memory satisfies P, a read gives a value whose pointers satisfy P.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.State.write_ok
theorems.says: A write of a value whose pointers satisfy P keeps every pointer in memory satisfying P.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.evalPlace_ptr
theorems.says: A place whose base local may be borrowed, or that goes through a dereference, evaluates to a pointer to frame 0 or to a local its frame's function may borrow.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.execStmt_okAt
theorems.says: A statement whose refs are of places that may be borrowed, or through a dereference, keeps every pointer in memory naming frame 0 or a borrowed local.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.step_borrows
theorems.says: Every step keeps the borrow invariant: memory holds only pointers to frame 0 or to a local the function of its frame may borrow, and no pointer names a frame not yet made.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.State.setSlot_comm
theorems.says: Replacements of two different slots commute.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.State.write_setSlot_other
theorems.says: A write to another slot commutes with the replacement of a slot.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.State.write_setSlot_same
theorems.says: A write of a whole slot gives the same state whatever the slot was replaced by before.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.execStmt_put
theorems.says: A statement that does not mention a local its function does not borrow does the same whatever that local's slot holds.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.execStmt_putFar
theorems.says: A statement does the same whatever a slot of a frame that is not running holds, when no pointer in memory is into it.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.execStmt_puts
theorems.says: A statement does the same through a list of replaced slots, each hidden and of another frame or of a local the statement does not mention.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.execStmt_absorb
theorems.says: A statement through a list of replaced slots gives its state with the slots it did not store to replaced: a store to a whole replaced local forgets it.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.stmtLive_dead
theorems.says: Under a liveness certificate the check accepts, a local dead before a statement is stored to whole by it, or is not mentioned and is dead after it.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.ret_puts
theorems.says: A return through a list of replaced slots: the entries that are the destination's whole slot leave the list, and those of the frame that returned replace nothing.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.callOn_puts
theorems.says: A call through a list of replaced slots: entering a function keeps the list, and an intrinsic's write of its destination forgets the entries that are its whole slot.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.run_refines_rel
theorems.says: When from related states the source's step is undefined or the two programs' steps are related, every run of the target refines the source's run from a related state.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.removeDead_refines
theorems.says: Global dead-store elimination under a liveness certificate the check accepts refines the program: every run is the program's, unless the program's is undefined, from every state the borrow invariant holds of whose frames are ordered.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.removeDead_call
theorems.says: Global dead-store elimination refines every call whose base slots and arguments have pointers into frame 0 only.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.removeDeadStoresChecked_preserves
theorems.says: Global dead-store elimination with its certificate is a rewrite of the witness validator: it keeps every call that ends, and not in undefined behaviour, whose base slots and arguments have pointers into frame 0 only.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.run_refines_inv
theorems.says: When every step of the target refines the step of the source on the states an invariant holds of, and the source's steps keep it, every run from such a state refines.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.checkBorrows_sound
theorems.says: A program checkBorrows accepts takes references only to locals its borrowed-set lists, or through a dereference.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.removeOverwritten_refines
theorems.says: Removing a store that its own block overwrites before its local is mentioned refines the program, from every state the borrow invariant holds of; the Rust DeadStoreElimination also removes stores dead by liveness across blocks and unwinding, which is not specified (ledger V11).

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.removeOverwritten_call
theorems.says: Removing a store its own block overwrites refines every call whose base slots and arguments have pointers into frame 0 only.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.validateWith_sound
theorems.says: The witness validator is sound: when a script of rewrites proved for every call takes one program to another, every call that ends, and not in undefined behaviour, gives the same outcome with the same fuel.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.validateWith_sound_frameZero
theorems.says: The same for any script, removeOverwritten and removeDead among its rewrites, for the calls whose base slots and arguments have pointers into frame 0 only.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.evalRvalue_sym
theorems.says: An rvalue of the scalar, move-free subset evaluates to the value of its symbolic expression over the block's initial locals, and leaves the state as it was.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.execStmts_sym
theorems.says: Executing a block's statements is the meaning of their symbolic trace: each expression evaluated in the block's initial state and written to its local.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.execStmts_same
theorems.says: Statement lists with one symbolic trace do the same from every state.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.symEq_sound
theorems.says: Programs whose blocks are equal or have one symbolic form run alike, for every fuel and every state.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.validateSym_sound
theorems.says: When a script of proved rewrites takes one program to a program symbolically equal to another, every call whose caller hands over pointers into frame 0 only, that ends and not in undefined behaviour, gives the same outcome.

theorems.name: Blaze.Mir.Opt.simplifyCfg_call
theorems.says: SimplifyCfg composed from the proved passes keeps every call that ends, and not in undefined behaviour: the same outcome with the same fuel.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.diff_correct
theorems.says: The meaning of diff c x e is the derivative of the meaning of e in variable x, wherever every node is inside its rule's domain.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.gradient_correct
theorems.says: Each entry of the gradient is the partial derivative in its variable.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.jacobian_correct
theorems.says: Each entry of the Jacobian is the partial derivative of its root in its variable.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.hessian_entry_correct
theorems.says: Differentiating a derivative again gives the second partial derivative, where the first derivative is inside the rules' domains.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.abs_tangent_at_kink
theorems.says: At 0 the generated tangent of abs is the argument's tangent times the choice.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.abs_choice_is_subgradient
theorems.says: A choice in [-1, 1] is a subgradient of the absolute value at 0.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.min_tangent_at_tie
theorems.says: At a tie the generated tangent of min is c * t0 + (1 - c) * t1.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.max_tangent_at_tie
theorems.says: At a tie the generated tangent of max is c * t0 + (1 - c) * t1.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.max_choice_is_subgradient
theorems.says: A choice in [0, 1] is a subgradient of max at a tie.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.min_choice_is_supergradient
theorems.says: A choice in [0, 1] is a supergradient of min at a tie.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.sqrt_tangent_at_kink
theorems.says: At 0 the generated tangent of sqrt is the choice times the argument's tangent (a convention: there is no subgradient).

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.select_tangent
theorems.says: The generated tangent of select is its taken arm's tangent.

theorems.name: BlazeDiff.rewrites_sound
theorems.says: Every fast_math rewrite of the simplifier is an identity over the reals under its stated condition.

theorems.name: theorems.bump_keeps_wf.spec.proof
theorems.says: The statement blaze generates from the theorem function bump_keeps_wf holds of its model: from a counter with hits at most its limit, bump does not panic and leaves hits at most the limit.

theorems.name: theorems.counting_ends.spec.proof
theorems.says: The statement blaze generates from the theorem function counting_ends holds of its model: for every n some fuel makes the loop return, with i equal to n.

theorems.name: queue.new_is_wf.spec.proof
theorems.says: The statement blaze generates from the theorem function new_is_wf holds of its model: a new bounded queue (a `Vec` and a limit) is well formed for every limit.

theorems.name: queue.offer_keeps_wf.spec.proof
theorems.says: The statement blaze generates from the theorem function offer_keeps_wf holds of its model: from every queue and item, offer does not panic and leaves a well-formed queue well formed (its `Vec::push` never passes the limit).

theorems.name: queue.take_keeps_wf.spec.proof
theorems.says: The statement blaze generates from the theorem function take_keeps_wf holds of its model: from every queue, take (a `Vec::pop`) leaves a well-formed queue well formed.

theorems.name: blaze_core.busy.next_is_bounded.spec.proof
theorems.says: The statement blaze generates from blaze-core's theorem function next_is_bounded holds of its model: for every number of tries and every time waited, busy::next does not panic and its wait is positive, at most the cap and at most what is left of the bound (so the waits of an exec that met ETXTBSY end, on the bound exactly).

theorems.name: blaze_core.busy.next_is_the_doubling_schedule.spec.proof
theorems.says: The statement blaze generates from blaze-core's theorem function next_is_the_doubling_schedule holds of its model: for every number of tries and every time waited, busy::next (one shift) gives the wait of busy::doubling (the loop that doubles and caps), which returns.

theorems.name: blaze_core.world.clock.a_timer_never_fires_early.spec.proof
theorems.says: The statement blaze generates from blaze-core's theorem function a_timer_never_fires_early holds of its model: for every clock, wait and reading, a timer the clock world allows fired waited at least its time (or its deadline did not fit a u64 and the reading is the last there is), the clock after the reading allows none before it, and nothing overflows or panics.

theorems.name: BlazeCore.World.DiskAllows.allows_orders
theorems.says: Of the disk world's model as the translator emits it from disk.rs: a cut `Disk::allows` accepts has one share per file, and if it keeps, whole or in part, a change of any file made after a barrier of any file completed, it keeps whole every change that barrier covers.

theorems.name: BlazeCore.World.DiskAllows.allows_total
theorems.says: `Disk::allows` neither panics nor runs out of fuel, for every disk and every cut.
